title: Shared drawers: First qualifying slip
summary: The input contains exactly two drawers. Produce the distinct readings present in both drawers, in increasing numeric order. Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.
descriptionMd:
Two departments have exchanged lists of reading tags for their shared equipment shelf. Rafi needs the first qualifying slip while the courier waits at the door. Later matches must not jump ahead in the tray.

The input contains exactly two drawers. Produce the distinct readings present in both drawers, in increasing numeric order.

Return the first value in the derived sequence that is at least k, or -1 if there is none. Return the value, not its index.

Implement sharedDrawersFirstQualifyingSlip(drawers, k). Use k exactly where specified above.
unitIntro: Set intersection. The input contains exactly two drawers. Produce the distinct readings present in both drawers, in increasing numeric order. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The input has exactly two rows, each containing at most 64 integers.

Target time O(n + d log d); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
